title: Intrinsic linewidths of confined phonons in few-layer hBN
authors: Aleksandar Radic, Jack Kelsall, Akshay Rao
abstract: Understanding lattice vibrations in two-dimensional (2D) materials is essential for controlling thermal transport, mechanical response, and energy dissipation in nanoscale devices. However, the intrinsic lifetimes of low-energy phonon modes, particularly those that are optically silent, remain largely unexplored. Here we use helium-3 spin-echo spectroscopy to resolve low-energy phonons at the surface of hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) and measure their intrinsic linewidths. We observe the flexural and Rayleigh wave modes and extract the bending rigidity of a quasi-freestanding hBN monolayer. We further report the simultaneous observation of multiple surface-confined interlayer shear modes whose energies agree closely with linear-chain model predictions. By resolving their intrinsic linewidths, we demonstrate a strong confinement-induced reduction in phonon lifetimes, with a near order of magnitude increase in linewidth between the four- and two-layer modes. The temperature dependence of the linewidths indicates that phonon-phonon scattering dominates between 160-360K, while the systematic broadening with decreasing layer number reveals the impact of confinement on phonon decay. These results reveal how reduced dimensionality affects the decay of interlayer shearing modes in hBN, providing direct insight into the phonon lifetimes, confinement effects, and dissipation pathways that govern the dynamical behaviour of two-dimensional materials.
summary: This work uses Helium-3 spin-echo spectroscopy to measure the intrinsic linewidths of low-energy phonon modes in few-layer hBN. The key finding is that reducing dimensionality strongly affects phonon decay rates, showing a dramatic increase in confinement-induced broadening for thinner films. This provides fundamental insights into how material structure governs energy dissipation pathways in 2D materials.
main_problem: The study aims to understand the intrinsic linewidths of low-energy, often optically silent, phonon modes in few-layer hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). This is crucial for controlling thermal and mechanical properties in nanoscale devices.
main_result: The researchers found a strong confinement effect, demonstrating that the phonon lifetime decreases significantly—by nearly an order of magnitude—when moving from four- to two-layer hBN modes. They also characterized temperature dependence dominated by phonon-phonon scattering at higher temperatures.
method: Helium-3 spin-echo (HeSE) spectroscopy was employed to measure the low-energy vibrational spectrum, which is advantageous because it avoids probe-induced heating common in optical techniques.
model_or_system: The physical system is few-layer hBN. Theoretical models include simple harmonic membrane–substrate coupling theory for flexural modes and the Linear Chain Model (LCM) used to predict interlayer shear mode energies.
key_observables: Phonon dispersion relations (flexural, Rayleigh wave, interlayer shear modes), intrinsic linewidths ($\gamma$), bending rigidity ($\kappa$), and temperature dependence of phonon decay rates.
important_parameters: Temperature range ($160-360 	ext{ K}$); layer number (2L, 3L, 4L); confinement strength; scattering mechanisms (phonon-phonon vs. defect-phonon).
main_assumptions: The HeSE technique is assumed to provide a surface-sensitive measurement free from optical selection rules or probe heating effects.
figures_summary: Figures show the quadratic dispersion of flexural modes, energy transfer spectra for interlayer shear modes at various temperatures, and plots detailing linewidths versus temperature for different layer numbers.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the need to measure intrinsic phonon lifetimes in 2D materials. It then details the use of HeSE spectroscopy to resolve specific low-energy modes (flexural/Rayleigh waves) and interlayer shear modes (ISMs). The core analysis focuses on comparing measured linewidths across different layer numbers and temperatures against theoretical predictions.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state phononics, the study of energy dissipation pathways ($\gamma$) in confined systems provides analogous insights to decoherence rates or coupling strengths in open quantum systems, particularly those involving lattice vibrations or phonons mediating interactions.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Dispersion of the flexural phonon mode at the surface of hBN along the ΓM direction. The flexural mode arises from simple harmonic coupling between a weakly bound (quasi-freestanding) monolayer and a substrate, and is well-described by an approximately quadratic dispersion (Eqn.1)[10, 12]. Individual points and uncertainties were extracted from Lorentzian fitting to energy transfer spectra (Figure A1) at sample temperature T = 360 K and tilt angle α = 135◦. All data shown here appear as annihilation (+∆E) features in energy transfer spectra. The shaded region repre- sents the 95% confidence interval of the fit to Eqn. (1).

Figure 2. Enegy transfer spectra of the 3L (blue) and 4L (red) interlayer shearing modes (ISMs) with single Lorentzian fits for sample temperatures 160 −360 K and tilt angle α = 129.1◦. Linewidth for each fit is shown in the legend of the respective panel. In Figure 3 we analyse the temperature dependence of these linewidths alongside the fitting of the 2L mode. Fits with high uncertainty are shown with dashed lines and are not used in the subsequent analysis. A 2nd-order polynomial background subtraction was applied to account for multi-phonon background contributions to intensity followed by a Savitsky-Golay filter (1st-order with window width 7) is used to remove high-frequency noise.

Figure 3. Linewidths of the 2–4L interlayer shearing modes (ISM) at the surface of bulk hBN from 160 −360 K. Inset shows the energy transfer spectrum of the 2L mode fit with a Lorentzian at 360 K and tilt angle α = 129.1◦yielding fre- quency ω2L = 4.65 meV and linewidth γ2L = (210 ± 40) µeV. The linear relationship between linewidth and temperature for the 3L and 4L modes indicates dominant phonon-phonon scattering while the constant offset corresponds to defect- phonon scattering[23].
